summary: Boundary County, Idaho lookout on Myrtle Peak: first structure 1925, Bosworth range-finding board 1933, destroyed 1955; a hiking guide describes remains of the tower.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1955; a hiking guide describes the remains of the tower on the peak

staffing.status: lookout personnel named: Evan Watson (1933) and Richard McAteer (1936); no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as a hike-in; a hiking guide describes a trail to the peak and mentions no closure. Public status is not confirmed by a land manager.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in per Idaho Fire Lookouts. A hiking guide describes trail #286 and says a high-clearance vehicle is required for part of the forest road to the trailhead.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com calls the 1925 structure a platform; Idaho Fire Lookouts calls it a tower. The story reports the first structure and both descriptions without choosing one.
Only firelookout.com dates a new tower at a different spot to 1934; the story presents it as that page's claim.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on 1955 destruction and the 1933 and 1936 names. They disagree on the 1925 structure (platform or tower) and only firelookout.com has the 1934 replacement. The 1929 fire is attributed to the 'Myrtle creek lookout' in the newspaper; the story does not say that is definitely this tower. Access is recorded only as hike-in (Idaho Fire Lookouts) plus a hiking account; public status is not confirmed by a land manager, so confirm with Kaniksu National Forest before stating access. The hiking guide is a 2017-era account and the remains were not verified on the ground. A YouTube video (not read) says a few timbers and some metal cables remain; use only after checking it.
